title: Stalks of cohomology sheaves
statement:
For $Q\in D(T_{\Et})$ and a geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$,

$$
\mathcal H^q(Q)_{\bar t}=\mathcal H^q(Q_{\bar t}),
$$

where $Q_{\bar t}$ denotes the pullback of $Q$ to the point.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], represent $Q$ by any cochain complex $C^\bullet$ of abelian sheaves on $T_{\Et}$. Put $Z^q=\Ker(d^q:C^q\to C^{q+1})$ and $B^q=\Im(d^{q-1}:C^{q-1}\to C^q)$. The identity $d^qd^{q-1}=0$ gives $B^q\subset Z^q$, and the cohomology definition gives $\mathcal H^q(Q)=Z^q/B^q$. No boundedness or injectivity of $C^\bullet$ is needed.

Write $S=(-)_{\bar t}$. Apply the exactness assertion of [prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact] to $0\to Z^q\to C^q\to B^{q+1}\to0$ and $0\to B^{q+1}\to C^{q+1}\to C^{q+1}/B^{q+1}\to0$: the second sequence makes $S(B^{q+1})\to S(C^{q+1})$ injective, so the first identifies $S(Z^q)$ with $\Ker S(d^q)$ and $S(B^{q+1})$ with $\Im S(d^q)$. Applying this with $q-1$ also gives $S(B^q)=\Im S(d^{q-1})$. Finally apply exactness to $0\to B^q\to Z^q\to Z^q/B^q\to0$. Thus $S(\mathcal H^q(Q))\cong S(Z^q)/S(B^q)=H^q(S(C^\bullet))$. These identifications use the indicated kernel inclusions and quotient maps, hence are canonical.

source.place: Tag 010N, lemma-exact-functor, kernel/image factorization in the proof; applied to the three displayed short exact sequences

proof.text: The calculation of step 2 is natural for chain maps: a map of complexes sends cycles to cycles and boundaries to boundaries, and the induced map on the quotient is the cohomology map on both sides of the comparison. If a chain map is a quasi-isomorphism, its maps on cohomology sheaves are isomorphisms, and applying $S$ preserves these isomorphisms; step 2 therefore shows that its termwise stalk is a quasi-isomorphism. By the localization definition of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], termwise $S$ thus defines the derived stalk functor, with $S(C^\bullet)$ representing the stalk of $Q$. The natural comparison descends too: it commutes with chain maps and hence with the inverses of quasi-isomorphisms in the localization. Now use only the statement of [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback] to identify this derived stalk with the inverse image $Q_{\bar t}$. Step 2 gives $\mathcal H^q(Q)_{\bar t}\cong\mathcal H^q(Q_{\bar t})$, the canonical identification denoted by equality in the statement, independently of the representative.
